models.name: Span-Wagner (1996) Helmholtz EOS
models.knownLimitations: Near-critical region (|T−Tc| < 2 K) uses nonanalytic terms; avoid at T < 220 K.

models.name: Peng-Robinson (1976) EOS with Li & Yan (2009) binary interaction parameters
models.citation: Peng, D.Y. & Robinson, D.B. (1976). Ind. Eng. Chem. Fundam. 15(1):59–64. k_ij from Li & Yan (2009) J. Supercrit. Fluids 50(2):143–150
models.knownLimitations: Use only when CO₂ stream contains CH₄, N₂, H₂S, or SO₂ impurities. Pure CO₂: use Span-Wagner.

models.name: Fenghour, Wakeham & Vesovic (1998)
models.citation: Fenghour, A., Wakeham, W.A. & Vesovic, V. (1998). J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 27(1):31–44. DOI: 10.1063/1.556013
models.knownLimitations: ±5–10% in the dense supercritical region vs. Laesecke & Muzny (2017); upgrade pending coefficient transcription.

models.name: Laesecke & Muzny (2017) NIST Reference Correlation
models.citation: Laesecke, A. & Muzny, C.D. (2017). J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 46(1):013107. DOI: 10.1063/1.4977429
models.knownLimitations: Implementation stub only. Full coefficient table transcription is a planned upgrade. Improves accuracy from ±5% to ±0.5% in the supercritical region.

models.name: CO₂ critical-point thresholds
models.citation: NIST WebBook (2023). NIST Standard Reference Database 69. Tc = 304.13 K, Pc = 7.377 MPa

models.name: Garcia (2001) NaCl/CaCl₂ correlation
models.citation: Garcia, J.E. (2001). LBNL-49023, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. Kell (1975) pure-water baseline; Bigg (1967) NaCl polynomial
models.knownLimitations: Polynomial fit valid 0–200°C, 0–15 mol/kg NaCl; extrapolates outside this range.

models.name: Constant brine viscosity (no correlation implemented)
models.citation: N/A (2026). Assumed 6×10⁻⁴ Pa·s, representative of formation brine at ~60°C and moderate salinity.
models.knownLimitations: No temperature, pressure, or salinity dependence. Use Batzle & Wang (1992) or Phillips et al. (1981) for T/P/S-sensitive cases. Planned PhD-era upgrade.

models.name: Duan & Sun (2003) Pitzer-type EOS
models.knownLimitations: 5-coefficient compact fit; ±5–10% vs full published EOS. For regulatory submissions use full Duan-Sun (2003) with all Pitzer terms.

models.name: Duan, Sun, Zhu & Chou (2006) multi-salt extension
models.citation: Duan, Z., Sun, R., Zhu, C. & Chou, I.-M. (2006). Marine Chemistry 98(2–4):131–139
models.knownLimitations: Ternary interaction (zeta) terms set to zero for screening accuracy; stored coefficients calibrated for MPa input.

models.name: Chapman-Enskog kinetic theory with tortuosity correction
models.citation: Duan, Z. & Sun, R. (2003). Base diffusivity ~2×10⁻⁹ m²/s; tortuosity τ=1.5 for sandstone. Chapman-Enskog T-scaling.
models.knownLimitations: Screening-level estimate; ignores salinity dependence on diffusivity.

models.name: MARS (Multivariate Adaptive Regression Splines) IFT model
models.citation: Olagunju, D.T. et al. (2026). MSc research, Universiti Teknologi PETRONAS (UTP), Malaysia. In preparation. Trained on 3,265 experimental CO₂-brine IFT datapoints from 16 independent laboratories across 4 continents.
models.knownLimitations: Two separate models: subcritical (16 terms, T<304.13 K) and supercritical (35 terms, T≥304.13 K). Applicability domain gated via conformal prediction intervals (80% PI). Scope: CO₂-brine IFT only; pure water and impure CO₂ streams not yet covered.

models.name: van Genuchten (1980) + Mualem (1976) model with Krevor et al. (2012) parameters
models.citation: van Genuchten, M.Th. (1980). Soil Sci. Soc. Am. J. 44(5):892–898. Mualem (1976) Water Resour. Res. 12(3):513–522; lab parameters from Krevor et al. (2012) WRR 48:W02544
models.knownLimitations: Berea/Fontainebleau sandstone parameters from Krevor et al. (2012); user-adjustable for other lithologies.

models.name: Brooks & Corey (1964) power-law kr model
models.citation: Brooks, R.H. & Corey, A.T. (1964). USDA Hydrology Papers 3
models.knownLimitations: Simpler power-law form; less accurate near residual saturations. Use van Genuchten-Mualem as primary for CO₂/brine systems.

models.name: Killough (1976) imbibition scanning + Land (1968) residual model
models.citation: Land, C.S. & Killough, J.E. (1976). SPE J. 16(1):37–48 (Killough); Land (1968) Trans. AIME 243:149
models.knownLimitations: Land coefficient C=5.0 for intermediate sandstone; adjust via sgrMax parameter for other lithologies.

models.name: Brooks-Corey (1964) drainage / imbibition curves
models.citation: Brooks, R.H. & Corey, A.T. (1964). USDA Hydrology Papers 3
models.knownLimitations: Pc capped at 10×Pe to avoid numerical blowup. Entry pressure Pe derived from MARS IFT output and caprock pore-throat radius.

models.name: Land (1968) residual saturation model
models.knownLimitations: Land coefficient C=2.5 in classical module; C=5.0 in VE solver (sandstone default). Adjust for carbonate or tight reservoirs.

models.name: Interfacial-area-limited mass transfer with Rayleigh convective onset (Riaz et al. 2006)
models.citation: Riaz, A., Hesse, M., Tchelepi, H.A. & Orr, F.M. (2006). J. Fluid Mech. 548:87–111. Duan & Sun (2003) for equilibrium solubility; Ennis-King & Paterson (2005) for dissolution rate scaling
models.knownLimitations: Convective enhancement factor Ra/Ra_crit where Ra_crit=4π²; screening-level estimate only.

models.name: Xu et al. (2004) geochemical kinetics
models.citation: Xu, T., Apps, J.A. & Pruess, K. (2004). Environ. Sci. Technol. 38(10):2790–2796
models.knownLimitations: Active only after year 50 (geochemical equilibration period); T-factor Arrhenius correction relative to 60°C.

models.name: Laplace capillary entry pressure model (Schowalter 1979, Berg 1975)
models.citation: Schowalter, T.T. (1979). AAPG Bulletin 63(5):723–760. Berg (1975) AAPG Bulletin 59(6):939–956; Pe = 2γ·cosθ/r_throat
models.knownLimitations: Uses MARS IFT output for γ; pore-throat radius r is a user input or lithology default. Screening-level only.

models.name: Theis (1935) transient radial flow well function
models.knownLimitations: Assumes infinite homogeneous aquifer, single fluid phase. Superseded by Nordbotten (2005) for two-phase CO₂ injection; retained for AoR baseline and single-phase validation.

models.name: Nordbotten, Celia & Bachu (2005) two-phase composite radial flow
models.citation: Nordbotten, J.M., Celia, M.A. & Bachu, S. (2005). Transp. Porous Media 58(3):339–360
models.knownLimitations: Analytical infinite-aquifer model. For bounded domains or k<100 mD, use the FD pressure solver for accurate BHP. Used for fast screening.

models.name: Peaceman (1978) equivalent well-block radius
models.citation: Peaceman, D.W. (1978). SPE-6893-PA
models.knownLimitations: r_eq = 0.1982·Δx for square cells; r_w = 0.1 m default wellbore radius.

models.name: Implicit 5-point finite-difference backward-Euler with conjugate-gradient solver
models.citation: Internal CarbonLens (2026). Matrix-free CG on 5-point SPD stencil; harmonic mean face transmissibilities; no-flow BCs. Replaces Nordbotten analytical for live 3D animation and bounded domains.
models.knownLimitations: CG convergence in 60–120 iterations for 60×60 grid; condition number ∼nx². For very low permeability (<1 mD) may need preconditioning.

models.name: Chabora & Benson (2009) pressure-threshold AoR delineation
models.citation: Chabora, E. & Benson, S.M. (2009). GHGT-9 Energy Procedia 1(1). EPA Class VI UIC Program Guidance, 40 CFR 146.84; threshold 6.9 kPa (1 psi)
models.knownLimitations: Bisection on Nordbotten (2005) composite ΔP to find threshold contour radius. Single-phase fallback: Theis radial diffusion rₐᴼᴿ = √(4Kt/φμc_t).

models.name: Vertical Equilibrium 2D FD solver (Nordbotten & Celia 2006; Gasda et al. 2009; Hesse et al. 2008)
models.citation: Nordbotten, J.M. & Celia, M.A. (2006). Water Resour. Res. 42:W01407. Gasda et al. (2009) Adv. Water Resour. 32:1322–1334; Hesse et al. (2008) J. Fluid Mech. 611:35–60
models.knownLimitations: Explicit forward-Euler upwind scheme; CFL-adaptive sub-stepping (~25 sub-steps/yr at 2000 mD). Numerical diffusion causes 4–37× more cells vs MRST implicit at trace-CO₂ threshold; use η>5m threshold for field comparison.

models.name: Hesse, Orr & Tchelepi (2008) self-similar gravity current
models.citation: Hesse, M.A., Orr, F.M. & Tchelepi, H.A. (2008). J. Fluid Mech. 611:35–60. DOI: 10.1017/S002211200800267X
models.knownLimitations: Buckley-Leverett fractional flow; two shocks (leading mobile, trailing residual). Assumes flat caprock; not valid for dipping or faulted structures.

models.name: DOE/NETL Goodman et al. (2011) volumetric capacity methodology
models.citation: Goodman, A. et al. (2011). Int. J. Greenhouse Gas Control 5(4):828–833. Cc: P10=0.0051, P50=0.020, P90=0.055
models.knownLimitations: Volumetric method gives P10–P90 range; not a dynamic simulation. Cc coefficients are statistical averages across US saline aquifers.

models.name: Kopp, Class & Helmig (2010) trapping efficiency decomposition
models.citation: Kopp, A., Class, H. & Helmig, R. (2010). Int. J. Greenhouse Gas Control 4(4):727–740
models.knownLimitations: E_geo, E_sweep, E_disp decomposition; sweep efficiency uses Buckley-Leverett end-point mobility ratio.

models.name: Shook & Mitchell (2009) flow-quality index sweep efficiency
models.citation: Shook, G.M. & Mitchell, K.M. (2009). SPE-124625-MS, SPE ATCE 2009
models.knownLimitations: Derived from tracer-based heterogeneity index (FQI). Dykstra-Parsons V_DP used as proxy for FQI; validated against layered aquifer studies.

models.name: Dykstra-Parsons log-normal permeability distribution with AoR heterogeneity scaling
models.citation: Dykstra, H. & Parsons, R.L. (1950). Secondary Recovery of Oil in the United States, API, p. 160–174. AoR scaling: r_AoR_corr = r_AoR × exp(σ²/4), σ = −ln(1−V_DP)
models.knownLimitations: Log-normal permeability distribution assumed. V_DP from user input or lithology default.

models.name: Hubbert & Willis (1957) minimum horizontal stress fracture pressure
models.citation: Hubbert, M.K. & Willis, D.G. (1957). Trans. AIME 210:153–166
models.knownLimitations: Poisson ratio ν=0.30 default; user-adjustable. MAIP = 0.9 × Pf per Bachu et al. (2007).

models.name: Mohr-Coulomb shear failure + Biot (1941) poroelastic coupling
models.citation: Jaeger, J.C., Cook, N.G.W. & Zimmerman, R.W. (2007). Blackwell Publishing. Streit & Hillis (2004) Energy 29(9–10):1445–1456; Byerlee (1978) friction law
models.knownLimitations: Slip tendency Ts = τ/σ_eff_n; 2D plane-stress; fault orientation from user input. Byerlee friction: μ=0.85 (σ_eff<200 MPa), μ=0.6 (>200 MPa).

models.name: Teatini et al. (2011) nucleus-of-strain elastic approximation
models.citation: Teatini, P. et al. (2011). J. Geophys. Res. 116:B08204
models.knownLimitations: Elastic approximation: δ ≈ (ΔP·h/E)·(1−ν²)·a; valid for flat surface, isotropic elastic halfspace.

models.name: Linear geothermal gradient
models.citation: N/A (2026). T(z) = T_surface + gradient·z; default 30°C/km (typical sedimentary basin). User-adjustable in FormationInputs.
models.knownLimitations: No radial temperature profile or Joule-Thomson correction in screening mode. Use full thermal simulator for injection near-wellbore cooling.

models.name: Sleipner 4D seismic and gravimetric monitoring benchmark
models.citation: Furre, A.-K. et al. (2017). Energy Procedia 114:3916–3926. Chadwick et al. (2004) Energy 29(9–10); Boait et al. (2012) JGR 117:B03309
models.knownLimitations: Model excludes 9 intra-formational shale baffles; uses bulk homogeneous Utsira parameters. BHP not comparable (shale baffles increase real injection pressure to ~33 MPa).

models.name: SPE Comparative Solution Project Case 11A
models.citation: Nordbotten, J.M. et al. (2024). Flemisch et al. (2024) benchmark comparison results
models.knownLimitations: Semi-analytical pressure and saturation; agrees within P10–P90 benchmark envelope.
